Research

Research toward
inspectable intelligence

We study how explicit task concepts—entities, relationships, states, and allowed actions—can work with learned patterns and recorded experience. We aim to test whether this structure can improve learning from limited examples and make results more reliable. Each claim needs controlled comparisons and independently checked outcomes.

October 2026 / Native research

Measured failures inform
the next experiment.

R6 / CUDA experiments

Learning limits, measured.

Two FP32 CUDA fits used 600 updates each with 54,014 parameters. Selected checkpoints achieved mathematics IID 1/96 (1.04%) and OOD 0/96; coding scored 0/96 in both regimes.

Physics target standardization reduced state error, but OOD and physical-law composition remained weak. One seed does not establish generalization.

R6.1 / Zero-update diagnostics

A correction to investigate.

Final-state GRU encoding attenuated early-token gradient access. Masked mean pooling restored that access without adding parameters in the measured probes.

No R6.1 retraining or Kaggle job was run in this diagnostic. Improved learned accuracy remains unestablished.

Separate engineering evidence

Hybrid capability has
its own provenance.

Candidate C extends supported computation; its 36/36 and 12/12 results are not native-model accuracy. No comparative native STEM score is claimed: those general Class 12-style inputs are outside the R6 research schema.

Focus areas

Understanding what the policy learns,
what the controller contributes,
and what execution can verify.

Coding

Repairing software through bounded edits, explicit repository state, and independent terminal tests. The lockbox contains 100 tasks evaluated under four conditions; differences in supervision and interactions limit causal comparisons.

Frozen coding protocol ↗

Task isolation, conditions, and evaluation boundaries.

Results and failure evidence ↗

Success, structural OOD performance, and retained failures.

Audit and reproducibility ↗

Inspect the preserved execution and evaluation record.

Numeric mechanisms

Controlled multiplication environments make carries, digit positions, and action constraints explicit. The v2 interventions separate neural readouts from deterministic controller behavior.

Controlled intervention study ↗

80 distinct tasks, three trained seeds, eight conditions.

Zero-weight controls ↗

Singleton legal-action masks can solve the procedure without learned weights.

Scientific gap closure ↗

Targeted replication and bounded coding telemetry.

Physics

Learning how objects move and interact from observed states and actions. V3 exposed severe long-horizon errors. R5.3 improves on frozen V3.1 references on a new panel, but structured learning still fails the predeclared superiority gates.

Physical world models ↗

The complete simulated study: motion, interactions, planning and independently verified negative findings.

Stability and generalization ↗

Object-centric states, pairwise interactions and multi-step supervision, evaluated at 8, 16 and 32 steps.

R5.3 findings and limits ↗

Inspect the original gates, per-seed results, calibration failures and the NO-GO decision.

Shared learning and composition

Testing whether learned transitions transfer between domains, and whether local rules compose into reliable procedures. Negative results remain part of the research record.

Shared evaluator and graph transitions ↗

V4 failed to demonstrate useful transfer; V5 qualification stopped before training.

Mathematical generalization ↗

R5.2 local correctness did not translate into reliable whole-task composition.

Current research kernel ↗

Explicit neural and tool provenance; R5.1 transfer findings and limits.

Verification and observability

We preserve executed transitions, distinguish hypothetical plans from actual outcomes, and test the limits of our evidence. Replay agreement establishes consistency with saved records; it does not establish task success.

Architecture ↗

Observations, state, proposals, actual results, and independent goals.

Computation tracing ↗

Recorded numeric computation and the limits of historical telemetry.

Research limitations ↗

Scope, unequal information, statistical limits, and unresolved questions.
